inOneSentence: An admin types an e-mail and the person joins the workspace by a link, without anyone creating accounts or sharing passwords by hand.

threeThings.t: Nobody creates accounts by hand anymore.
threeThings.p: The admin types an e-mail. The person sets their own password when they open the link.

threeThings.t: A link lives seven days, once.
threeThings.p: After that it shows as expired; the admin sends a new one. Opened twice, the second open says it was already used.

threeThings.t: Whoever opens the link first gets in.
threeThings.p: A forwarded link is a risk you accepted for the first customers; a second factor may come later.

howSteps.p: The admin types the person's e-mail on the pending invites screen.
The system e-mails a link that works for seven days.
The person opens it, chooses a password and is in the workspace.
Unopened after seven days, the link says it expired; the admin can resend.

stories.S-001: The admin invites by e-mail; a link goes out, and inviting a member again sends nothing.
stories.S-002: The person opens the link, sets a password and is in; an expired link just says so.

outPlain: Two things stay out. Bulk invites from a spreadsheet are future direction. Roles at invite time are not built: everyone comes in as a member.
betsPlain: One bet is unchecked: that seven days is enough for people to open the link. The e-mail provider's delivery time holds by its published SLA.
inferredPlain: One assumption, confirmed: a week means seven calendar days.
reviewPlain: One round, three findings. One decision was yours (the forwarded link); the author fixed one wording; one mechanism goes to the design; one finding was dismissed with the sentence that closes it.

decisions.1:disc-reviewer-boundary#1: A forwarded link lets whoever opens it first in; you accepted the risk for now.
